items.name: Definition of Done
items.summary: Establishes the uniform completion criteria that every backlog item must satisfy before it can be counted as delivered, ensuring teams across the enterprise hand over work of consistent, production-ready quality.

subs.title: Code Complete
subs.description: All development work for the item is finished, merged to the integration branch, and free of known unfinished stubs or TODO placeholders. Partial implementations may not be carried forward into a subsequent sprint under the same story.

subs.title: Tested
subs.description: The item has passed unit, integration, and applicable regression testing, with automated coverage added or updated for the changed behavior. Defects found during testing must be resolved or formally accepted by the product owner before the item closes.

subs.title: Documented
subs.description: Relevant documentation is updated alongside the change, including technical design notes, runbooks, API references, and any user-facing or operations material affected. Documentation updates are part of the story, not deferred follow-up work.

subs.title: Reviewed
subs.description: At least one qualified peer has completed a code review and recorded approval in the source control tool. Review comments classified as blocking must be addressed before merge.

subs.title: Deployable
subs.description: The change builds cleanly in the CI pipeline and can be promoted to production without manual intervention beyond the standard release process. Items that require unscheduled environment work or unresolved configuration are not done.

subs.title: Accepted
subs.description: The product owner has reviewed the working functionality against the acceptance criteria and formally accepted it in the work management tool. Acceptance is the final gate before the story contributes to velocity.

items.name: Definition of Ready
items.summary: Defines the minimum quality bar a backlog item must meet before a team commits to it in sprint planning, protecting sprints from vague or blocked work and keeping delivery predictable.

subs.title: Acceptance Criteria
subs.description: Each story carries explicit, testable acceptance criteria agreed with the product owner before planning. Criteria must describe observable behavior so testers and developers share one definition of success.

subs.title: Dependencies Identified
subs.description: Upstream and cross-team dependencies, including those on policy administration, claims, or shared data platforms, are identified and recorded on the item before commitment. Dependent teams must have acknowledged the need or the item stays in refinement.

subs.title: Sized
subs.description: The team has estimated the item using its agreed sizing method, and stories too large to complete within a single sprint are split before they enter planning.

subs.title: No Blockers
subs.description: Known impediments such as pending access, unresolved design questions, or missing test data are cleared or have a dated resolution plan before the item is pulled into a sprint. Items with open blockers remain on the refinement backlog.

items.name: Scrum Ceremonies
items.summary: Requires every Scrum team to conduct the full set of ceremonies — Sprint Planning, Daily Standup, Sprint Review, and Retrospective — in line with the Scrum Guide, with consistent attendance, timeboxes, and recorded outcomes so that delivery rhythm and inspection points are uniform across teams.

items.name: Sprint Cadence
items.summary: Standardizes the length and rhythm of sprints across delivery teams so that planning, reporting, and cross-team coordination operate on a shared, predictable calendar.

subs.title: Two-Week Sprints
subs.description: All Scrum teams operate on a two-week sprint length. Deviations require PMO approval and are limited to teams with a documented operational constraint, such as regulatory release windows.

subs.title: Consistent Start and End Days
subs.description: Sprints begin and end on the same weekdays enterprise-wide, allowing program-level events, dependency syncs, and reporting cycles to be scheduled against a common boundary.

subs.title: Sprint Goals Documented
subs.description: Every sprint carries a written sprint goal recorded in the work management tool at planning. The goal states the business outcome the sprint advances and is referenced at the sprint review to assess whether it was met.

items.name: Velocity Tracking
items.summary: Governs how teams measure and use their delivery throughput, giving the PMO and product owners an evidence-based foundation for forecasting and commitment rather than intuition.

subs.title: Velocity Calculated
subs.description: Each team computes velocity every sprint from accepted story points only, using a consistent method maintained in the work management tool. Stories rejected or carried over do not count toward the sprint's velocity.

subs.title: Used for Planning
subs.description: Sprint and release commitments are sized against the team's rolling average velocity, typically over the last three to six sprints. Commitments that materially exceed demonstrated velocity require explicit product owner sign-off and a stated rationale.

subs.title: Trend Monitored
subs.description: Velocity trends are reviewed at retrospectives and in PMO health checks to detect sustained decline, volatility, or inflation. Significant shifts trigger a root-cause discussion rather than silent re-baselining.

subs.title: Capacity Planning
subs.description: Velocity is reconciled with actual team capacity each sprint, adjusting for planned leave, holidays, production support rotations, and onboarding. Capacity-adjusted forecasts are the basis for any external delivery date communicated to stakeholders.

items.name: Change Control
items.summary: Defines the disciplined process for altering an approved project scope, schedule, or budget, ensuring changes are deliberate decisions made at the right authority level rather than uncontrolled drift.

subs.title: Change Request Process
subs.description: Any proposed deviation from the approved baseline is documented as a formal change request in the PMO tool, with a unique identifier, requester, description, and justification. Verbal or email-only changes are not recognized.

subs.title: Impact Assessment
subs.description: Before a decision, each change request receives an assessment of its effect on scope, schedule, cost, resources, and risk, including downstream impact on regulatory commitments or dependent initiatives. The assessment is attached to the request record.

subs.title: Approval Authority
subs.description: Changes are approved at the level defined in the project's governance matrix, with thresholds based on cost and schedule impact. Requests exceeding the project manager's delegated authority escalate to the sponsor or steering committee.

subs.title: Baseline Updates
subs.description: Once approved, the project baseline, plan, and financial forecast are updated to reflect the change, and subsequent status reporting measures performance against the revised baseline. Superseded baselines are retained for audit traceability.

items.name: Project Closure
items.summary: Sets out the controlled wind-down activities required to formally end a project, ensuring value is confirmed, knowledge is retained, and people and budget are released cleanly back to the organization.

subs.title: Deliverable Acceptance
subs.description: All contracted deliverables are formally accepted in writing by the sponsor or designated business owner against the success criteria in the charter. Outstanding items are either accepted with documented exceptions or transferred to a named owner with a plan.

subs.title: Lessons Learned
subs.description: A lessons-learned session is held with the core team and key stakeholders before disbandment, and the findings are recorded in the PMO repository in a searchable form. Recurring themes are reported to the PMO for process improvement.

subs.title: Knowledge Transfer
subs.description: Operational documentation, support procedures, and system knowledge are handed over to the receiving run teams, with sign-off from the accepting manager. Transfer is complete only when the run organization confirms it can support the solution without project staff.

subs.title: Resource Release
subs.description: Project staff, contractors, and funded capacity are formally released on a communicated schedule, with assignments updated in the resource management system. Contractor end dates and access revocations are coordinated with vendor management and security.

items.name: Intake Process
items.summary: Controls how new demand enters the portfolio, ensuring every proposed investment is justified, achievable with available capacity, and ranked transparently before work begins.

subs.title: Business Case Required
subs.description: No initiative enters the portfolio without an approved business case covering the problem statement, expected benefits, cost estimate, and alignment to enterprise strategy. The depth of the case scales with investment size per the PMO's tiering guidance.

subs.title: Value Assessment
subs.description: Each request is evaluated for quantified business value, whether expense reduction, premium growth, loss-ratio improvement, regulatory necessity, or risk mitigation. Value claims must identify the accountable business owner who will be measured on realization.

subs.title: Capacity Validation
subs.description: Intake confirms that the delivery teams, subject-matter experts, and funding needed for the request exist or can be sourced before approval. Requests that cannot be staffed are queued rather than approved into an over-committed portfolio.

subs.title: Prioritization Criteria
subs.description: Approved requests are scored against the portfolio's published prioritization criteria at intake so they enter the backlog with a defensible relative ranking. Criteria and weights are maintained by the portfolio governance board, not adjusted per request.

items.name: Portfolio Reviews
items.summary: Establishes the recurring governance forum where leadership inspects the health of the full investment portfolio and acts on problems early, keeping delivery aligned with strategy and capacity.

subs.title: Monthly Portfolio Review
subs.description: The portfolio governance board meets monthly to review all active initiatives, with a standard pack covering financials, delivery status, benefits, and risk. Attendance by accountable executives or their empowered delegates is mandatory.

subs.title: Health Indicators
subs.description: Every initiative is assessed against a standard set of health indicators spanning schedule, budget, scope, resourcing, and benefits confidence, using PMO-defined thresholds. Indicator definitions are uniform so initiatives can be compared on equal terms.

subs.title: Escalation Triggers
subs.description: Predefined conditions, such as consecutive red statuses, budget variance beyond tolerance, or a missed regulatory milestone, automatically escalate an initiative to the board's exception agenda. Escalation is rule-driven and not subject to project-manager discretion.

subs.title: Replanning Process
subs.description: Initiatives that fail review may be directed into a structured replan covering revised scope, schedule, cost, and benefits, with a deadline for returning to the board. The board's options explicitly include pausing or terminating initiatives that no longer justify investment.

items.name: Prioritization Framework
items.summary: Provides the objective method by which competing investment demands are ranked, so that funding and delivery capacity flow to the work that best serves the enterprise rather than to the loudest sponsor.

subs.title: Weighted Scoring Model
subs.description: All candidate initiatives are scored through a single weighted model with published criteria and weights approved by the portfolio governance board. Scores are recorded in the portfolio tool and refreshed when an initiative's assumptions materially change.

subs.title: Strategic Alignment
subs.description: Scoring includes an explicit measure of how directly an initiative advances stated enterprise and business-line strategies, such as digital distribution, claims modernization, or retirement-business growth. Initiatives unable to map to a strategic objective receive the minimum alignment score.

subs.title: ROI Consideration
subs.description: Expected financial return, including payback period and net benefit over the planning horizon, is a weighted factor in every ranking. Mandatory regulatory work is flagged separately so compliance obligations are not forced to compete on ROI alone.

subs.title: Resource Constraints
subs.description: Final sequencing reflects real constraints on scarce skills, shared platforms, and change capacity in business operations. A high score does not guarantee immediate start if the required teams or environments are committed elsewhere.

items.name: Gate Reviews
items.summary: Defines the stage-gate checkpoints at which a project must prove its readiness to proceed, giving governance bodies structured decision points to continue, redirect, or stop investment.

subs.title: Phase Gate Criteria
subs.description: Each lifecycle phase has published entry and exit criteria maintained by the PMO, and a project may not advance until the exit criteria for its current phase are demonstrably met. Criteria cover delivery readiness, financial position, and risk posture.

subs.title: Deliverable Checklist
subs.description: A standard checklist of required artifacts, such as the approved design, test summary, or operational readiness assessment, is completed and evidenced before each gate. Missing artifacts must be waived in writing by the gate authority, with the waiver recorded.

subs.title: Approval Workflow
subs.description: Gate decisions follow a defined workflow with named approvers, and the outcome, whether approved, approved with conditions, or held, is recorded in the PMO tool. Conditional approvals carry dated actions that are tracked to closure.

subs.title: Lessons Learned
subs.description: Each gate review captures lessons from the completed phase while they are fresh, feeding both the project's own next phase and the PMO's cross-project knowledge base. Gate-level lessons supplement, not replace, the closure retrospective.

items.name: Project Charter
items.summary: Requires every project to begin with an authorized founding document that establishes its mandate, boundaries, and measures of success before significant spend or staffing occurs.

subs.title: Sponsor Approval
subs.description: The charter is signed by an accountable executive sponsor with authority over the affected business area and budget. Work beyond preliminary scoping may not start until sponsor approval is recorded.

subs.title: Scope Definition
subs.description: The charter states what the project will and will not deliver, including affected products, channels, systems, and business units. Explicit out-of-scope statements are required to prevent later disputes over boundaries.

subs.title: Success Criteria
subs.description: Measurable success criteria are defined at chartering, tied where possible to operational or financial metrics such as cycle time, expense ratio, or customer satisfaction. These criteria become the basis for deliverable acceptance and benefits tracking.

subs.title: Assumptions and Constraints
subs.description: Material assumptions, such as vendor availability or regulatory timelines, and binding constraints, such as fixed compliance dates or capped funding, are documented in the charter. Each is revisited during planning and converted to a risk if it proves uncertain.

items.name: Project Planning
items.summary: Specifies the core planning artifacts every project must produce after chartering, so that work, dates, people, risks, and stakeholder communication are managed deliberately from day one.

subs.title: WBS or Backlog
subs.description: The full scope is decomposed into either a work breakdown structure or a prioritized product backlog, depending on the delivery method. Every deliverable in the charter must trace to elements of this decomposition.

subs.title: Schedule or Roadmap
subs.description: A baselined schedule with milestones and dependencies, or an equivalent release roadmap for agile delivery, is maintained in the approved planning tool. Key dates with regulatory or contractual force are flagged as fixed and protected through change control.

subs.title: Resource Plan
subs.description: The plan names the roles, skills, and allocation levels the project needs over time, including business SMEs from underwriting, claims, or actuarial functions whose availability is often the binding constraint. Confirmed commitments are recorded with the supplying managers.

subs.title: Risk Register
subs.description: A risk register is established during planning, seeded from the charter's assumptions and constraints and from PMO lessons on similar initiatives. The register is a living artifact reviewed on the project's standing governance cadence.

subs.title: Communication Plan
subs.description: A communication plan identifies stakeholders, what information each group receives, the channel, and the frequency, from steering packs to frontline operations briefings. It also defines who may communicate externally where regulators, agents, or policyholders are affected.

items.name: Status Reporting
items.summary: Standardizes how project health is communicated to stakeholders and governance bodies, ensuring leaders receive timely, comparable, and honest information on which to base decisions.

subs.title: Weekly Status Report
subs.description: Every active project issues a status report each week in the PMO's standard template, published in the portfolio tool by the agreed deadline. Reporting continues through quiet periods so absence of news is itself visible.

subs.title: RAG Status
subs.description: Overall health and the schedule, budget, scope, and resource dimensions are each rated red, amber, or green against PMO-defined thresholds. Ratings reflect the defined criteria, and downgrades may not be suppressed or softened for audience comfort.

subs.title: Milestones
subs.description: The report shows progress against baselined milestones, including completed, upcoming, and slipped dates with revised forecasts. Movement of any regulatory or contractual milestone is highlighted explicitly.

subs.title: Risks and Issues
subs.description: Top risks and open issues are summarized with their current severity, owner, and the action being taken, drawn directly from the project's RAID log. New high-severity entries since the prior report are called out.

subs.title: Decisions Needed
subs.description: The report states the specific decisions required from the sponsor or steering committee, the options considered, the recommendation, and the date by which a decision is needed to avoid impact. Stale undecided items escalate per the governance matrix.

items.name: Capacity Planning
items.summary: Governs how the organization forecasts and balances delivery capacity against portfolio demand, preventing over-commitment of teams and surfacing staffing conflicts before they damage delivery.

subs.title: Quarterly Capacity Forecast
subs.description: Resource managers produce a rolling quarterly forecast of available capacity by team and skill group, net of run-the-business obligations, leave, and attrition assumptions. The forecast is reconciled against approved portfolio demand before each quarterly planning cycle.

subs.title: Allocation Visibility
subs.description: Current and planned allocations for every delivery resource are maintained in the resource management system and visible to the PMO and supplying managers. Side arrangements that commit people outside the system are prohibited.

subs.title: Conflict Resolution Process
subs.description: When two or more initiatives compete for the same people or teams, the conflict is raised through a defined process that resolves it using portfolio priority order. Unresolved conflicts escalate to the portfolio governance board rather than being settled by informal negotiation.

items.name: Time Tracking
items.summary: Requires consistent recording of effort across the delivery organization so that project costs, capitalization decisions, and future estimates rest on actual data rather than assumption.

subs.title: Time Captured Weekly
subs.description: All project staff, including contractors, submit time in the enterprise timekeeping system by the weekly cutoff, with manager approval following on the published schedule. Chronic late submission is reported to the PMO and the individual's manager.

subs.title: Project and Task Level
subs.description: Time is recorded against the specific project and task or workstream codes from the approved plan structure, not against generic buckets. This granularity supports accurate cost allocation and the capitalization treatment required for financial reporting.

subs.title: Actuals Versus Estimate Analysis
subs.description: Project managers compare recorded actuals against estimates at least monthly, investigating variances beyond tolerance and feeding the findings into forecasts and future estimating models. Persistent estimation bias is surfaced to the PMO for calibration.

items.name: Issue Management
items.summary: Defines how realized problems on a project are captured and driven to closure, ensuring issues receive a named owner and a deadline instead of lingering unmanaged.

subs.title: Issue Logging
subs.description: Any problem actively impacting scope, schedule, cost, or quality is recorded in the project's issue log within the governance tool, with a clear description, date raised, and severity. Issues discussed in meetings but never logged are treated as a process breach.

subs.title: Ownership
subs.description: Every open issue has a single named owner accountable for driving resolution, assigned at the point of logging. Ownership may transfer, but an issue may never sit unowned or be assigned to a group.

subs.title: Target Resolution Date
subs.description: Each issue carries a committed resolution date proportionate to its severity, and the date is tracked at the project's standing reviews. Slipped dates require a revised plan and an explanation, not silent extension.

subs.title: Escalation Path
subs.description: Issues that exceed the project manager's authority or breach their resolution date escalate along the documented path, from project manager to sponsor to steering committee. The escalation route and thresholds are defined in the project's governance plan at initiation.

items.name: Risk Management
items.summary: Establishes the proactive discipline for anticipating threats to delivery before they materialize, so projects in a risk-conscious insurance enterprise manage their own exposure with the same rigor the business applies to underwriting.

subs.title: Risk Identification
subs.description: Risks are actively identified throughout the project lifecycle, through planning workshops, standing team reviews, and triggers such as scope changes or vendor events. Anyone on the project may raise a risk, and identification is treated as a contribution rather than a criticism.

subs.title: Probability and Impact Assessment
subs.description: Each risk is scored for likelihood and consequence using the PMO's standard scales, producing a severity rating that drives review frequency and management attention. Impact assessment considers financial, schedule, regulatory, and reputational dimensions.

subs.title: Mitigation Plans
subs.description: Risks above the defined severity threshold require a documented response, whether mitigation, transfer, acceptance, or avoidance, with actions assigned to named owners and dates. Acceptance of a high-severity risk requires sponsor sign-off.

subs.title: RAID Log
subs.description: Risks, assumptions, issues, and dependencies are maintained together in a current RAID log within the governance tool, reviewed at least at every status cycle. The RAID log is the single authoritative record feeding status reports and gate reviews.

items.name: ART Sync
items.summary: Governs the weekly coordination rhythm of each Agile Release Train, keeping teams aligned on PI objectives between planning events and ensuring obstacles and cross-team entanglements are dealt with promptly.

subs.title: Weekly ART Sync
subs.description: The Release Train Engineer convenes a weekly sync combining the Scrum of Scrums and PO sync perspectives, attended by team representatives and product owners. The session reviews progress against PI objectives and adjusts plans where reality has diverged.

subs.title: Impediment Resolution
subs.description: Impediments raised at the sync that cannot be resolved within a team are owned by the RTE and tracked on a visible impediment board until cleared. Items blocked beyond an agreed age escalate to the ART's leadership or Lean Portfolio Management.

subs.title: Cross-Team Dependencies Tracked
subs.description: Dependencies between teams on the train, and with external parties such as platform, data, or vendor teams, are maintained on the ART planning board and reviewed at every sync. At-risk dependencies are renegotiated explicitly rather than discovered at the system demo.

items.name: Inspect & Adapt
items.summary: Mandates the structured improvement event at the close of each Program Increment, ensuring every Agile Release Train measurably learns from its own performance rather than repeating the same problems PI after PI.

subs.title: PI Retrospective
subs.description: Each train holds a PI-level retrospective as part of the Inspect and Adapt event, reviewing the PI system demo, objective achievement, and quantitative measures such as predictability. Participation spans teams, product management, and ART leadership.

subs.title: Problem-Solving Workshop
subs.description: The event includes a facilitated root-cause workshop on the most significant problems surfaced, using structured techniques such as fishbone analysis or five whys. Output is a small set of well-understood causes with proposed countermeasures, not a grievance list.

subs.title: Improvement Backlog Maintained
subs.description: Agreed improvement actions are written as backlog items, entered into the ART backlog, and given capacity in the next PI plan. The RTE reports on the status of prior improvement items at the following Inspect and Adapt so actions cannot quietly evaporate.

items.name: PI Planning
items.summary: Sets the quarterly planning event as the heartbeat of each Agile Release Train, aligning all teams on shared objectives and a realistic, dependency-aware plan that leadership and teams jointly commit to.

subs.title: Quarterly PI Planning
subs.description: Every Agile Release Train conducts a PI Planning event each quarter with all teams, product management, and business owners participating, in person or via the approved distributed format. The event follows the standard agenda, including business context, draft plan reviews, and management problem-solving.

subs.title: Objectives Set
subs.description: Each team drafts PI objectives describing the business outcomes it will deliver, and business owners assign value to them during the event. Committed and stretch objectives are distinguished, and the aggregated train objectives are published after the event.

subs.title: Dependencies Identified
subs.description: Teams surface dependencies on one another and on external groups during plan reviews and place them on the program board with agreed dates. A plan with unowned or unscheduled dependencies is not accepted as final.

subs.title: Confidence Vote
subs.description: The event closes with a confidence vote in which every participant rates the achievability of the plan. An average below the threshold triggers rework of the plan in the room before the train commits, and individual low votes are heard rather than overridden.

items.name: Vendor Management
items.summary: Governs how third-party delivery partners are engaged and overseen on projects, protecting the carrier's spend, delivery commitments, and contractual position across its supplier base.

subs.title: Statement of Work and Contract Management
subs.description: All vendor delivery work operates under an executed SOW or contract that defines deliverables, rates, acceptance terms, and key personnel, negotiated with procurement and reviewed by legal. Work beyond the contracted scope requires an amendment before it begins.

subs.title: Milestone Tracking
subs.description: Contractual milestones and deliverable due dates are loaded into the project plan and tracked alongside internal work, with formal acceptance recorded for each completed milestone. Slippage against contracted dates is reported in project status and assessed for remedy provisions.

subs.title: Performance Monitoring
subs.description: Vendor performance is reviewed on a regular cadence against agreed measures such as quality, responsiveness, staffing stability, and SLA attainment, with findings documented in the vendor governance record. Sustained underperformance triggers a corrective action plan with the supplier's account leadership.

subs.title: Invoicing
subs.description: Vendor invoices are validated against the SOW, approved time records, and accepted milestones before payment is authorized by the budget owner. Discrepancies are disputed within the contractual window, and invoice status is reconciled in the project's financial tracking.
